=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py: enumerate_workspace() directory check at `if not allowed(name + "/placeholder.py") or (Path(directory) / child).is_symlink():` | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The directory validation rejects the `.github` directory even though `snapshot()` copies `.github/workflows/` and `.github/actions/` files into the workspace.
  WHY: `snapshot()` uses `git ls-files` on a real checkout, which returns `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` (among others). The file passes `allowed()` because `parts[:2] == (".github", "workflows")` is in the allowed set, so it is copied to the workspace. Then `refresh()` (called at the end of `prepare`) invokes `enumerate_workspace(workspace)`. When `os.walk` yields the root directory with `child=".github"`, the skip condition `rel == Path(".") and child.startswith(".") and child != ".github"` is False (because `child == ".github"`), so the directory is not skipped. The next check calls `allowed(".github/placeholder.py")`, which returns False because `len(parts) == 2 < 3` and `parts[:2] == (".github", "placeholder.py")` is not in the allowed pair set. The function raises `ValueError("unsafe workspace directory")`, the helper exits 1, and `prepare` fails. Every real PR that has `.github/workflows/` or `.github/actions/` files — which is every PR this isolation is meant to protect — hits this path. The test `test_review_isolation_workspace_transfer_and_hostile_paths` does not exercise it because its synthetic host has no `.github` directory.
